info.name: World Service
info.description:
Covers map bootstrap, zones, rooms, coordinates, barricades, resource-nodes, zombie-spawns and the unlock flow for the World Service (see cpr/PAD-team1/world-service/README.md section 10 for the auth/role table this mirrors).

Every request goes through the API Gateway (`base_url`, default http://localhost:8080): since 2.0.0 the service only accepts requests the Gateway forwarded, so calling it directly gives 401. This collection mints its own JWTs via the collection-level pre-request script (HS256 with `exp`, signed with the Gateway's secrets), and every run generates fresh, non-colliding map/zone/room/course data, so importing it and clicking "Run" is enough — no manual token-pasting or id edits needed.

Before running, set the `jwt_secret` / `service_jwt_secret` collection variables to the `JWT_SECRET` / `SERVICE_JWT_SECRET` values from the team's `.env` (the ones the Gateway runs with), or pass them with newman's `--env-var`. The defaults are `change_me`, the placeholders in `.env.example`.

Temporary, until the Gateway is in the team's docker-compose.yaml: to call the service directly, set `base_url` to the service (http://localhost:4004) and `gateway_secret` to `GATEWAY_SECRET` from `.env`; the pre-request script then adds the identity headers the Gateway would send. Leave `gateway_secret` empty to go through the Gateway.

exec: // A run starts at the collection's first request (Create Map (bootstrap with seed zone)): it gets a fresh
// run_id and forgets the ids the previous run created, because the Postman app keeps
// collection variables between runs. Every later request reuses them, so two runs in a
// row never collide (no 422 on re-created data, no progress carried over).
// Minimal HS256 JWT signer using Postman's bundled CryptoJS — lets this collection
// mint its own valid player/moderator/service tokens instead of needing them pasted
// in by hand before every run.
// The Gateway verifies every token: HS256, signed with the Gateway's JWT_SECRET (player
// tokens) or SERVICE_JWT_SECRET (service tokens, sub "service:<name>"), and exp is required.
signJWT({ sub: "postman-player-" + runId, roles: ["player"], type: "player", iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, jwtSecret)
signJWT({ sub: "postman-mod-" + runId, roles: ["player", "moderator"], type: "player", iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, jwtSecret)
signJWT({ sub: "service:exam-service", roles: ["service"], type: "service", iat: now, exp: now + 300 }, serviceSecret)
// TEMPORARY, until the Gateway is in docker-compose.yaml: with `gateway_secret` set (the
// GATEWAY_SECRET from .env) and `base_url` pointing straight at the service, send the
// headers the Gateway would add, built from this request's own token. Leave `gateway_secret`
// empty to go through the Gateway.
